question.text: How many AIS-visible commercial ship crossings of the Strait of Hormuz will hormuz.now record for 26 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number displayed as the headline 'commercial crossings' count on hormuz.now's daily archive page for 26 November 2026, https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-26 (the same daily totals are listed at https://hormuz.now/data). The snapshot is the value shown on that page at 2026-11-27 12:00 UTC; any later revision of the figure is ignored. That archive page is authoritative: where it disagrees with hormuz.now's news page, status page or daily briefing email — which have at times reported different numbers for the same day — the archive page governs. For example, if the page shows '6 commercial crossings', the question resolves to 6. If the page is not yet showing a complete-day figure at the snapshot time, the first complete-day figure subsequently shown on that page is used (and later revisions still ignored). If hormuz.now publishes no count for 26 November 2026 at all, the question is annulled.
question.fine_print: The counted figure is hormuz.now's own AIS-based 'commercial crossings' total — AIS-visible commercial ships (cargo ships and tankers of 80 m or more) crossing its counting line, counted once per direction — as defined at https://hormuz.now/methodology. Small-craft crossings are excluded, and the inbound/outbound and tanker sub-figures are not used. Only crossings occurring between 00:00 and 23:59 UTC on 26 November 2026 count. A figure presented as an in-progress count for the day (e.g. 'so far today') is not a complete-day figure.

research:
I haven't made a forecast, only gathered the facts. **Main point:** nothing settles the question yet. hormuz.now's live series started on 19 Oct and has stayed between 4 and 13 complete-day crossings a day. Some numbers in the question's background no longer match the archive. 11 Nov now reads **13** on its archive page, not 4. The table that had "4 (11 Nov), 6 (12 Nov)" looks like 10 Nov and 12 Nov.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The page for 26 Nov doesn't exist yet. hormuz.now's daily CSV (/api/daily.csv, one row per UTC day since 19 Oct 2026) lists these complete days: 9 Nov **6**, 10 Nov **4**, 11 Nov **13**, 12 Nov **6**, 13 Nov **5**, 14 Nov **6**, 15 Nov **6**. 16 Nov is partial: 3 crossings by 08:38 UTC. [CSV](https://hormuz.now/api/daily.csv)
- 2026-11-15: The archive page title reads "15 November 2026: 6 Ship Crossings". It also lists 8 small-craft crossings, which don't count. [page](https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-15)
- 2026-11-11: The archive page now reads "13 Ship Crossings", not the 4 given in the background. 10 Nov reads 4. So either the background mixed up dates or the archive figures get revised later. That matters because the question fixes the 27 Nov 12:00 UTC snapshot. [11 Nov](https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-11), [10 Nov](https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-10)
- 2026-11-16: status.json shows a 7-day average of 6.7 (about 7.9% of normal), 6 crossings in the last 24 hours, and a "live" feed. PortWatch data runs only to 8 Nov (3 that day, 7-day average 3.9). [status.json](https://hormuz.now/status.json)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles or nearly settles the result. 26 Nov is 10 days away.
- hormuz.now's status reads "Restricted, severely restricted" and hasn't changed since 19 Oct. [news](https://hormuz.now/news)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15/16: The IRGC (Iran's Revolutionary Guard) says three tankers hit mines on 14-15 Nov. It says two sank, and that they were running with AIS off on unauthorised routes. I haven't confirmed the sinkings independently. [newtalk](https://newtalk.tw/news/view/2026-11-16/1071356), [noticiasaominuto](https://www.noticiasaominuto.com/mundo/3084515/dois-petroleiros-afundam-se-no-estreito-de-ormuz-diz-irao)
- 2026-11-15: UKMTO (the UK's maritime trade reporting agency), citing Indian authorities, reports a tanker attacked heading eastbound just before the strait. The crew is safe. [india.com](https://www.india.com/news/world/tanker-attacked-in-arabian-gulf-near-strait-of-hormuz-all-crew-safe-indian-shipping-authorities-report-to-ukmto-8545186/)
- 2026-11-13: Windward counted 9 transits, all AIS-dark. Iran's blacklist stands at 240 ships. Kpler puts oil flows at about 8.3m barrels a day, around 48% of pre-war. The UN Security Council met with no deal. [hormuz.now news](https://hormuz.now/news)
- 2026-11-12: JMIC Update 113 keeps the threat level at SEVERE. It reports US Navy figures of about 34 US-assisted transits a day over 8-11 Nov, mostly invisible on AIS. Trump said "We don't need a deal with Iran." [news](https://hormuz.now/news)
- 2026-11-10: Iran's security chief said the strait won't reopen until the US meets its conditions. On 31 Oct Iran had cut its reopening plan from seven days to two. [news](https://hormuz.now/news)

## 4. Base rates
- hormuz.now complete days from 20 Oct to 15 Nov (27 days): 7, 11, 6, 9, 6, 4, 8, 5, 6, 11, 13, 12, 10, 5, 7, 7, 9, 13, 5, 5, 6, 4, 13, 6, 5, 6, 6. [api/traffic](https://hormuz.now/api/traffic)
  - Mean about 7.6, median 6, range 4-13.
  - Values of 4-6 came up on 14 of 27 days (52%). Values of 10 or more came up on 6 days (22%).
- Trend: the 7-day average peaked at about 9.3 (1-4 Nov) and has fallen to about 6.6. Since 12 Nov the days have been flat at 5-6, despite the attacks.
- No zero days since live counting began. Earlier dates show 0 only because the tracker didn't exist before 19 Oct.
- Monthly hormuz.now averages: Oct 7.5 (13 days), Nov 7.1 (15 days). PortWatch shows about half that: Mar 3.2, Apr 7.1, May 3.9, Jun 12.9 (partial reopening), Jul 10.2, Aug 4.7, Sep 3.6, Oct 3.8, Nov 3.5.
- Seasonality: the pre-crisis PortWatch average usually fell from October to November: 2021 80.8 to 83.9, 2022 101.1 to 84.8, 2023 95.2 to 76.9, 2024 90.0 to 83.2, 2025 89.4 to 67.4. Today's traffic is about 8% of normal and driven by the conflict, so the seasonal pattern probably matters little.

## 5. Other forecasts
None of these markets settles on hormuz.now. The weekly Kalshi and Polymarket markets look like they use PortWatch-style counts, judging by their price levels, but I haven't checked their rules.
- Kalshi, week of 16-22 Nov total: "Above 25" at 0.47, "Above 20" at 0.74, "Above 30" at 0.17. That implies roughly 3.5-4 a day.
- Polymarket, week of 16 Nov total: "26+" at 0.485. Peak day that week: "6+" at 0.66, "8+" at 0.27.
- Polymarket, "Avg. # of ships end of November": 0-4 at 0.865, 5-9 at 0.115.
- Kalshi, highest single day in November: "at least 8" at 0.71, "at least 10" at 0.18. hormuz.now has already recorded 13 this month, so this market clearly uses a different source.
- Polymarket, return to normal by 31 Jan 2027: 0.095.
- I found no expert forecast for hormuz.now's daily count.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Mining or attack claims continuing near the strait (14-15 Nov) could put more ships off crossing, or push more of them to go dark, which lowers the AIS count. So far the daily count hasn't fallen below 5 after these incidents.
- Any US-Iran deal under the two-day reopening plan, or a new escalation or closure, before or on 26 Nov. Nothing is scheduled. Trump's 12 Nov remarks point away from a quick deal.
- JMIC advisory updates (roughly weekly), PortWatch's weekly release (Tuesday 17 Nov, and 24 Nov), and possible revisions to hormuz.now's archive figures before the 27 Nov 12:00 UTC snapshot.
- 26 Nov is a Thursday. Weather isn't a material factor, and I didn't find a relevant forecast.

Sources: [hormuz.now data](https://hormuz.now/data), [daily.csv](https://hormuz.now/api/daily.csv), [status.json](https://hormuz.now/status.json), [api/traffic](https://hormuz.now/api/traffic), [news](https://hormuz.now/news), [15 Nov](https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-15), [11 Nov](https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-11), [10 Nov](https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-10), [newtalk](https://newtalk.tw/news/view/2026-11-16/1071356), [india.com](https://www.india.com/news/world/tanker-attacked-in-arabian-gulf-near-strait-of-hormuz-all-crew-safe-indian-shipping-authorities-report-to-ukmto-8545186/), [noticiasaominuto](https://www.noticiasaominuto.com/mundo/3084515/dois-petroleiros-afundam-se-no-estreito-de-ormuz-diz-irao), [AA](https://aa.com.tr/en/us-israel-iran-war/hormuz-ship-traffic-stays-limited-as-only-4-commercial-vessels-transit-in-24-hours/3927525), [gCaptain](https://gcaptain.com/shipping-traffic-through-hormuz-still-largely-halted/)

I've pulled hormuz.now's own data files and checked recent news, and I'm writing up the findings now.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16 (08:39 UTC): hormuz.now's daily file (https://hormuz.now/api/daily.csv) runs from 19 Oct 2026. Recent complete-day totals: 2 Nov 5, 3 Nov 7, 4 Nov 7, 5 Nov 9, 6 Nov 13, 7 Nov 5, 8 Nov 5, 9 Nov 6, 10 Nov 4, 11 Nov 13, 12 Nov 6, 13 Nov 5, 14 Nov 6, 15 Nov 6. 16 Nov is marked partial, with 3 so far. [csv](https://hormuz.now/api/daily.csv)
- 2026-11-16: The 15 Nov archive page shows "6 Ship Crossings": 2 inbound tankers, 3 outbound bulk carriers and 1 inbound container ship, plus 8 small-craft crossings that are not counted. [page](https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-15)
- 2026-11-16: status.json gives a 7-day average of 6.7, 47 crossings in the last 7 days, status "restricted" (about 8% of normal), and ships waiting: 504 on the Oman side and 106 on the Gulf side. [status](https://hormuz.now/status.json)
- One discrepancy you should know about: the 11 Nov archive page now shows **13** crossings, not the 4 given in the question background. The 4 matches 10 Nov in the CSV, so the background probably has the dates off by one. It could also mean the archive page gets revised after the fact, which would matter for the 27 Nov 12:00 UTC snapshot. The background's "13 Nov: 4 so far" ended the day at 5. [11 Nov page](https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-11)
- The 26 Nov page will appear at https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-26. The CSV's partial_day flag shows whether a day is complete.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The day in question is 10 days away.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Iranian media and the Jerusalem Post carry IRGC claims that more tankers caught fire on 15-16 Nov. The IRGC says the ships had turned off their AIS and were crossing with US help. Reuters could not verify this. [newscord](https://newscord.org/article/irans-navy-reports-tanker-fire-after-mine-hit-east-of-strait-of-hormuz--Story_20261116_Twomoreoiltankershitfdf2291f)
- 2026-11-15: The IRGC says two tankers hit mines in the southern strait and one supertanker (2m barrels) sank. UKMTO separately reported, via Indian authorities, an attack on an eastbound tanker just before the strait, with the crew safe. [anews](https://www.anews.com.tr/middle-east/2026/11/15/iran-says-2-oil-tankers-hit-mines-near-strait-of-hormuz-1-sinks), [india.com](https://www.india.com/news/world/tanker-attacked-in-arabian-gulf-near-strait-of-hormuz-all-crew-safe-indian-shipping-authorities-report-to-ukmto-8545186/)
- About 2026-11-10/12: US officials say the US escorted 40 ships in one day, a wartime high. Many of these appear to sail with AIS off. That fits Windward's count (8 of 10 transits dark on 12 Nov) and explains why hormuz.now's AIS-only count barely moved. [arabnews](https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/iran-says-supertanker-with-2-million-barrels-of-oil-sank-in-gulf-3012053)
- 2026-11-10: UKMTO's weekly count was 170 outbound and 155 inbound. UANI reported US-facilitated transits averaging 30.3 a day. [UANI](https://www.unitedagainstnucleariran.com/node/46596)
- Diplomacy looks stalled: on 21 Oct Araghchi said the strait won't be "open to everyone" until the US accepts Iran's terms. Lloyd's List's next Hormuz brief is due 19 Nov. [LLI](https://www.lloydslistintelligence.com/resources/blog/strait-of-hormuz-brief-5-november-2026)

## 4. Base rates
- 20 Oct to 15 Nov (27 complete days, leaving out 19 Oct, which shows 0 and looks like a start-up artefact): mean 7.6, median 6, range 4-13. Days at 4: 2. Days at 5: 5. Days at 6: 7. Days at 7-9: 6. Days at 10 or more: 7. [csv](https://hormuz.now/api/daily.csv)
- Last 14 days (2-15 Nov): mean 6.9. Last 7 days: 46-47 total, about 6.6 a day. Monthly average from hormuz.now: 7.5 in Oct (13 days), 7.1 in Nov so far.
- The series has calmed down: 12-15 Nov came in at 6, 5, 6, 6, even with the attacks. Highs of 13 show up about once a week (30 Oct, 6 Nov, 11 Nov).
- 26 Nov is a Thursday. Earlier Thursdays: 22 Oct 6, 29 Oct 11, 5 Nov 9, 12 Nov 6. I found no clear weekday pattern.
- Seasonality: in PortWatch's normal years, November averaged 67-85 transits a day (2022: 84.8, 2023: 76.9, 2024: 83.2, 2025: 67.4), down from October. That drop is tiny next to the crisis effect. hormuz.now has no earlier years. PortWatch during the crisis: Sep 3.6, Oct 3.8, Nov (8 days) 3.5. [traffic api](https://hormuz.now/api/traffic)

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of these markets resolves on hormuz.now's daily count. Their levels (weekly totals of about 25, a November average of 0-4) look like PortWatch-based resolution, which runs about half of hormuz.now. Check each market's rules before using them.
- Polymarket, week of 16 Nov total: 26+ at 48.5%, 30+ at 24.5%. Peak day that week: 6+ at 66%, 8+ at 27%. End-of-November average: 0-4 at 86.5%.
- Kalshi, week of 16-22 Nov: above 25 at 47%. Highest single day in November: at least 9 at 40%, at least 10 at 18%. That is consistent with PortWatch, since hormuz.now has already recorded 13.
- I found no expert forecast of hormuz.now's daily figure.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More mine and tanker attacks look likely. The question is whether they cut AIS-visible crossings or mainly push ships to go dark (the IRGC says the ships hit were dark).
- US escort tempo, and whether the 504 ships waiting on the Oman side start moving with AIS on.
- Any talks via Pakistan, Qatar or Vance that lead to a reopening or a new closure.
- 19 Nov: Lloyd's List brief. 17 and 24 Nov (Tuesdays): PortWatch updates.
- Weather: I did not check a forecast. Late November in the strait is usually calm, apart from occasional shamal winds.

(a) **Time left:** 26 Nov is 10 days away. The snapshot is taken 27 Nov 12:00 UTC, about 11 days from now.
